messages:
maya: Quick check — we need to pick a default surface for the new internal inference routing API. My vote: gRPC protobufs between services, JSON at the edge via a small gateway. Performance + typed schemas.
jc: Agreed on gRPC for service-to-service. Concern: console + partners rely on easy HTTP/JSON. How do we avoid double-maintenance? :thinking_face:
taylor: Telemetry/quotas angle: if we do gRPC internally and transcode at gateway, we must ensure route-level metrics and quota attrs survive. Envoy transcoding drops some headers by default. Need consistent span propagation.
nina: Proto-first + generated JSON shim seems reasonable. Problems to call out: streaming RPCs don't map cleanly to HTTP/1 JSON, and path/verb semantics get messy. Also watch out for repeated fields & sparse patch semantics.
maya: Right — streaming is rare for our inference control plane (mostly unary). We do have long-polling for job status though. Could keep that as a separate HTTP endpoint if needed.
jc: Another option: keep a minimal gateway that simply proxies HTTP->gRPC with JSON transcoding, no business logic. That keeps routing policy decisions centralized (region/capacity). But we then need to version the gateway contract.
taylor: For telemetry, please ensure gateway emits unified route keys: service, method, model_variant, route_policy. We need those in console dashboards to break down latency and cost per route. Also quota triggers must use the same composite key the control plane uses.
sam: On rollouts/UX: SDK consumers want stable endpoints and clear upgrade path. If we swap proto shapes under-the-hood we need compatibility guarantees and a canary flag in console. Canary looks like: 5% traffic to v2, auto rollback on error rate/latency.
nina: Implementation sketch: protos in repo/inference/proto/*.proto, generate server stubs + openapi for the gateway. Use google.api.http annotations for simple mapping. Example: ```proto\nservice Routing {\n  rpc RouteRequest(RouteReq) returns (RouteResp) {\n    option (google.api.http) = { post: "/v1/route" body: "*" };\n  }\n}\n```\nRemember to annotate required fields for validation.
maya: Good call. Also, for quota propagation we'll attach x-rdwd-route and x-rdwd-tenant headers at gateway. But those headers must be added to gRPC metadata so all downstream services can read them.
jc: Keep header names short and stable. Add a fallback: if header missing, consult the token introspection service to recompute attributes. We need a telemetry signal to surface when header population fails.
taylor: Tracing: gateway should inject traceparent / baggage. Services should not create new root spans. Also sample debug traces on canary routes.
sam: Can we wire console to show canary metrics automatically? Add a rollout tab: percent, start ts, error threshold, latency p95. If exceeded, button to rollback.
nina: One more gotcha: JSON->proto mapping will accept unknown fields, but proto3 ignores them. We should run strict validation in the gateway and return 400 for unknown fields to avoid silent data loss.
maya: Ops question: what about per-model quota enforcement? Do we enforce at gateway (easy) or at model-serving cluster (accurate)? Gateway enforcement risks being bypassed if internal calls are made.
jc: Enforce at both: gateway for fast rejection & cost control, authoritative enforcement at model-serving with counters stored in central quota service. Gateway should check a local cache and call quota service asynchronously for final accounting.
taylor: Add metrics: quota_check_latency, quota_rejected_local, quota_rejected_authoritative. Console dashboard should show these per-tenant and per-model.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: maya pushed proto-first-gateway branch to staging at 4949991222 :rocket: 
sam: Cool — plan for rollout: 1) API schema freeze, 2) implement gateway transcoding + strict validation in staging, 3) enable telemetry headers + tracing, 4) run integration tests for quotas, 5) canary to 5% for 24h, monitor p50/p95 and error rate.
nina: Also add a lint step that ensures all new protos include google.api.http and at least one example in the docs folder.
maya: Action items: jc -> write gateway design doc (incl. header mapping table) by EOD Wed; nina -> add proto linter rule; taylor -> dashboard mockups for route/model breakdown; sam -> rollout plan + console button mock; i'll open a follow-up thread for long-polling job status mapping.
jc: +1. If no objections I'll send out the design doc link here when ready.
taylor: One quick question: auth — are we using JWT in edge and forwarding token as bearer metadata, or perform token exchange at gateway?
maya: Edge keeps JWT, gateway verifies and attaches short-lived internal token (mtls-backed) to downstream calls. That lets services avoid public token parsing.
sam: Sounds good. I'll draft the canary thresholds and add them to the doc.
maya: Thanks all. Keeping the default: gRPC internal, JSON gateway transcoding with strict validation and robust telemetry. We'll iterate on streaming case separately. :thumbsup:
